catalog_locator: sec. 5.1.3 'Overview of varietal description format', p. 94 (group-level presyllable/stress statement); sec. 9.1 'Phong (Ponthai)', pp. 233-240: 9.1.1.2 'Notable features' pp. 234-235, 9.1.2 'Tone Categories' Table 9.1 p. 235, 9.1.3 'Sandhi & Coarticulation' p. 240.
catalog_quote: Tangsa-Nocte varieties typically have lexical tone. [...] The same applies to most Tangsa-Nocte varieties. The presyllable is toneless and unstressed, and in certain lexical items may be a reduced form of a tonal morpheme which has become a presyllable through compounding. [...] For the purposes of this thesis, presyllables have been marked with a zero tone, indicated by a subscript 0. || [9.1.1.2 Notable features, pp. 234-235] Phong has a number of notable features. While it follows the same tone categorisation as the other Tangsa-Nocte varieties, there are cases where words have changed tone category. [...] Regressive tonal assimilation in Phong is complete; the tone of the first syllable in a two-syllable compound will be entirely neutralised to a mid-level contour, such that it will be described by speakers as a third-tone word in that context but — if applicable – deriving from a different toneme. [...] In cases where an originally third-tone syllable is followed by another syllable of any tone in the same prosodic word, final aspiration is elided. || [9.1.3 Sandhi & Coarticulation, p. 240] In bisyllabic words, when a first or second tone syllable precedes another syllable of any tone, the first syllable becomes a mid-level contour resembling a third tone.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Ponthai (Phong) is a four-tone language (T1 low falling creaky, T2 mid delayed-falling modal, T3 mid level breathy, T4 short checked). The only remark bearing on stress is a group-level one: in the sesquisyllabic (C@-CV(C)) words typical of Tangsa-Nocte the presyllable (a prefix or a reduced first morpheme) is toneless and unstressed, so prominence lies on the major (final) syllable; in Phong bisyllabic compounds the tone of the first syllable is fully neutralised to a mid-level contour while the second keeps its tone. No source opened states a word-stress rule for Ponthai as such.
new_statements.exceptions: Presyllables that are reduced forms of tonal morphemes (compounding); in Phong, first- and second-tone first syllables of compounds are neutralised to a third-tone-like mid level, and final aspiration of third tone is elided non-finally.
new_statements.domain_note: The stress statement is generic ('most Tangsa-Nocte varieties'), not specific to Phong; the Phong section is about lexical tone on monosyllables in citation form (elicited in Wagun Ponthai, Changlang, Oct 2015, two consultants) and tone sandhi in two-syllable compounds. Domain is the phonological word (sesquisyllable / compound); no phrase-level stress discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog pont1258 'Ponthai' = the variety its speakers call Phong (also Phongtai/Pontai), officially 'Tangsa' in Changlang district and 'Nocte' in Tirap district; van Dam 2018 sec. 9.1 describes the Wagun Ponthai (Changlang) dialect plus one Tirap speaker and reports the two as mutually intelligible with only intonational differences. All quoted material is under the name 'Phong'. No ISO code (NOCODE_Ponthai).

sources.note: Family-level only: Patkaian varieties share a sesquisyllabic C@CV[CN] syllable structure with schwa-release presyllables (prefixes or reduced first morphemes of compounds); no stress statement; cites Dutta 2023 'A Descriptive Grammar of Phong' (Gauhati University PhD).

sources.citation: Dutta, Niharika. 2023. A descriptive grammar of Phong. PhD thesis, Gauhati University, Department of Linguistics (guide Jyotiprakash Tamuli). xv, 177 p. (Glottolog: 271 pp.).
sources.note: The only full grammar of Ponthai/Phong; Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description; chapter 2 presumably phonology and the most likely place for a first-hand statement on word stress vs tone. Chapter files exist on Shodhganga (05_chapter etc.) but are served only via port 8443, could not be reached by automated download and all proxies tried.
